answer: Policies are written in mesa, settled in lotus, and nadir lists every payout. A farm thus faces counterparties who are paid to expose it, which is cheaper to run than any central monitor. Peers may post insurance against an identity's behaviour and collect 14% of its slashed stake when it misbehaves, creating a market that profits from finding fraud. Scaling to 621 identities multiplies that fee by 321 with no matching gain in influence. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
